questions.question: Explain the different types of social behavior in fishes with suitable examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the different types of social behavior in fishes with suitable examples.
  • Shoal: A shoal is a loose group of fishes that stay together mainly for social reasons
  • such as protection, feeding, or mating, but without synchronized movement or
  • uniform direction.
  • School: A school is a highly organized and synchronized group of fishes that swim
  • together in the same direction, maintaining uniform spacing and movement.
  • Colony : A colony refers to a group of fishes that live together in a defined area for
  • nesting, breeding, or shelter but are not necessarily moving together.
  • Cluster : A cluster is a compact aggregation of fishes formed temporarily, usually as a
  • defensive or resting behavior.
  • Briefly mention the properties and functions

questions.question: Describe the role of excretion in maintaining ionic balance in both shrimps and bivalves.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the role of excretion in maintaining ionic balance in both shrimps
  • and bivalves.
  • Excretory organs: antennal (green) glands located at the base of the antennae.
  • These glands help remove nitrogenous waste (mainly ammonia) and regulate ions
  • like Na⁺, K⁺, and Cl⁻.
  • In marine shrimps, the glands help eliminate excess salts absorbed from seawater.
  • In freshwater shrimps, they help conserve salts and expel excess water by producing
  • dilute urine.
  • Excretion and Ionic Regulation in Bivalves
  • Bivalves : excretory organs are paired kidneys (nephrid ia) located near the
  • pericardium.
  • They excrete nitrogenous waste mainly as ammonia.
  • Kidneys also help regulate ionic concentration in the haemolymph.
  • Marine bivalves maintain osmotic balance by adjusting ionic exchange across gills
  • and nephridia.
  • Freshwater bivalves produce dilute urine to expel excess water while retaining salts.

questions.question: Explain the mechanism of respiration in Teleosts? / [CO1, CO2] [6x5 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the mechanism of respiration in Teleosts?
  • Gills are located in the gill chambers on each side of the pharynx, protected by
  • operculum. Each gill consists of: Gill arches, Gill filaments, Secondary lamellae (site
  • of gas exchange) Rich blood supply and thin epithelium allow efficient diffusion of
  • gases. The mouth opens and the buccal cavity floor lowers , increasing its volume.
  • Water enters the buccal cavity. The opercular cavity remains closed during this
  • phase. The mouth closes , and the buccal floor rises , decreasing cavity volume .
  • Opercular valves open , allowing water to flow over the gills and out through the
  • opercular openings. Gas exchange occurs as: O₂ diffuses from water into blood , CO₂
  • diffuses from blood into water. Blood in the secondary lamellae flows in the opposite
  • direction to the water current. This counter-current mechanism maintains a
  • concentration gradient, maximizing oxygen absorption efficiency.

questions.question: Describe the role of the stomach, gastric mill, hepatopancreas, midgut, and hindgut in the digestion and absorption of food in shrimp.
questions.solution_html:
• . Describe the role of the stomach, gastric mill, hepatopancreas, midgut, and
  • hindgut in the digestion and absorption of food in shrimp.
  • Stomach: Divided into: Cardiac and pyloric chambers
  • Function: Mechanical digestion and filtration, Cardiac stomach: Receives food,
  • performs grinding, Pyloric stomach: Filters fine particles to midgut
  • Gastric Mill : Location: Inside cardiac stomach , Structure: Three chitinous oss icles
  • (tooth-like plates) , Function: Mechanical trituration of food , Ensures only small
  • particles pass to pyloric region.
  • Hepatopancreas: Combined liver + pancreas, Function: Secretes digestive enzymes –
  • protease, amylase, lipase, Also involved in Absorption, storage, and metabolism
  • Midgut: Receives: Enzymes from hepatopancreas , Function: Chemical digestion and
  • absorption of nutrients , Absorbs Amino acids, sugars, fatty acids, glycerol ,
  • Adaptation: Presence of microvilli for increased surface area
  • Hindgut: Function: Water and ion reabsorption , Forms: Fecal pellets for elimination,
  • Lined with: Chitin for protection

questions.question: Describe various types of growth in finfishes and explain their importance in fisheries biology . [10x1 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe various types of growth in finfishes and explain their importance in
  • fisheries biology
  • Growth – permanent increase in size, weight, or volume of a fish over time.
  • Caused by cell division, enlargement, and tissue accumulation.
  • Types of Growth in Finfishes
  • A. Absolute Growth
  • Measures total increase in length or weight over time.
  • Formula: W2-W1 .
  • t2-t1
  • Indicates overall change in body size.
  • B. Relative Growth
  • Describes growth of one body part relative to another or to body size.
  • relative growth = W2-W1
  • Relative Growth rate is expressed as W2-W1
  • W1(t2-t1)
  • C. Isometric Growth
  • All parts grow at the same rate, maintaining same body proportions.
  • Cube Law
  • In length–weight relationship, b = 3.
  • Indicates balanced and uniform growth.
  • D. Allometric Growth
  • Unequal growth of body parts.
  • Positive allometry: one part grows faster (b > 3).
  • Negative allometry: one part grows slower (b < 3).
  • Importance of Growth Studies in Fisheries Biology
  • Age and Growth Estimation – determines fish age using scales, otoliths, etc.
  • Stock Assessment – helps estimate population and maximum sustainable
  • yield (MSY).
  • Fishery Management – identifies optimum size for capture and recruitment.
  • Aquaculture Practices – selection of fast-growing species, optimizing feed and
  • culture conditions.
  • Environmental Indicator – growth rate reflects water quality and habitat
  • conditions.
